findings.evidenceJa: 胸に刻んでおいてください
findings.governingReading: Saber asks Shirou to engrave the warning in his heart from this moment onward.
findings.explanation: The English weakens an embodied permanent injunction to ordinary recollection.

findings.highlight: the girl who fought with you as your sword until the very end
findings.evidenceJa: 最後まで君の剣であってくれた少女
findings.governingReading: The girl fought beside Shirou and remained or consented to be his sword through the end.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the sword role but weakens the benefactive willingness in あってくれた.

findings.highlight: There has to be a meaning to why you survived that hell
findings.evidenceJa: 生き延びた事には意味がある
findings.governingReading: The fact that Shirou survived has meaning.
findings.explanation: The English turns meaning located in survival into a demand for a causal reason why he survived and repeats “hell.”

findings.highlight: There has to be a meaning to why you must keep living
findings.evidenceJa: 生き延びたからには意味がある
findings.governingReading: Because Shirou survived, his continued existence must be made meaningful.
findings.explanation: The English changes the consequence of having survived into a reason he must remain alive.

findings.highlight: one person was saved by the sacrifice of everyone else
findings.evidenceJa: 一人分だけ、救える席が出来ただけだ
findings.governingReading: Everyone else’s sacrifice merely created one available place in which a single person could be saved.
findings.explanation: The English promotes the opening of a rescue place into an accomplished saving and makes the imagined transaction factual.

findings.highlight: a superhero that can save anyone
findings.evidenceJa: 誰をも救える“正義の味方”
findings.governingReading: Shirou felt compelled to become an “ally of justice” capable of saving everyone.
findings.explanation: The English substitutes the culturally and thematically different “superhero” and weakens 誰をも toward anyone.

findings.highlight: denied his battle because it was wrong
findings.evidenceJa: 自らの戦いが間違っていたと否定し
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu repudiated his own struggle as mistaken after destroying the Grail.
findings.explanation: The English’s causal wording suggests he denied that the battle occurred or denied it because of an independently established wrongness.

findings.highlight: you were left alone on the path
findings.evidenceJa: その道も、いつか一人きりになった
findings.governingReading: In time, that shared path became one Shirou walked alone.

findings.highlight: died, leaving the dream to you
findings.evidenceJa: 君に夢を見て亡くなった
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu died placing his dream and hope in Shirou.
findings.explanation: The English changes his hope invested in Shirou into a dream deliberately bequeathed to him.

findings.governingReading: The line should retain the pause in Kiritsugu’s “Yeah… I’m relieved.”
findings.explanation: The English runs the words together and removes the exhausted pause.

findings.highlight: If you are to deny everything you’ve done
findings.evidenceJa: おまえが今までの自分を否定するのなら
findings.governingReading: Archer warns that if Shirou repudiates the self he has been until now, the resulting debt will judge him.
findings.explanation: The English changes rejection of identity into rejection of past deeds.

findings.evidenceJa: その罪は必ず、おまえ自身を裁くだろう
findings.governingReading: The written sin is read as the debt or tab incurred by Shirou’s choice, and it will assuredly judge Shirou himself.
findings.explanation: The English loses the debt/sin double reading, certainty, and reflexive emphasis.

findings.highlight: I have to atone for it using all my life
findings.evidenceJa: 一生をかけて贖い続けなくてはいけない
findings.governingReading: Shirou must continue making atonement over the course of his entire life.
findings.explanation: The English uses the unnatural phrase “using all my life,” which can suggest expending life as an instrument.

findings.highlight: The me that was killed will feed on me
findings.evidenceJa: 虫食いのように、生きた自身を食んでいくだけ
findings.governingReading: The killed self will eat away at the living self like worm damage.
findings.explanation: The English omits both the worm-eaten simile and the killed/living contrast.

findings.governingReading: The writing names a saint’s burial while the reading supplies “shield,” superimposing Archer’s shroud and protection against death.
findings.explanation: The English keeps only the spoken shield reading and loses the burial layer.

findings.highlight: Archer’s arm will eat away at me
findings.evidenceJa: 繋がっているかぎり確実に侵食し
findings.governingReading: For as long as Archer’s arm remains connected, it will certainly continue its erosion.
findings.explanation: The English omits both the attachment condition and certainty.

findings.highlight: A girl that longed for her father, but lived seeking revenge
findings.evidenceJa: 復讐だけを心の糧にして時間を過ごしてきた少女
findings.governingReading: Illya passed her years with revenge as the sole sustenance of her heart.
findings.explanation: The English changes emotional sustenance and exclusivity into pursuing revenge, and adds an unsupported contrast with longing for her father.

findings.highlight: She almost cried, but smiled and swallowed her words so that we could live together
findings.evidenceJa: 一緒に暮らそう、という言葉を、泣きそうな笑顔で飲み込んだ
findings.governingReading: With a smile near tears, Illya swallowed her response to the invitation “let’s live together,” knowing the two could not live long together.
findings.explanation: The English makes swallowing her words serve the purpose of living together, reversing the reason she cannot accept the invitation.
